title: Hydrographic control of phytoplankton community composition: insights from winter monsoon observations along the west coast of India
content:
Abstract
The west coast of India, in the eastern Arabian Sea, is highly productive, yet the dynamics of winter-monsoon phytoplankton remain underexplored. This study assessed spatial variability in phytoplankton composition, abundance and ecological indices, and their relationship with hydrographic drivers along a transect from Veraval to Kanyakumari. Surface samples from six stations were analysed for temperature, salinity, pH, total alkalinity (TA), dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), nutrients and phytoplankton composition, abundance and indices. A clear north–south gradient was observed, with northern stations (Veraval, Mumbai) exhibiting higher salinity (35.5), nutrients (5.04 μmol L−1; phosphate 1.84 μmol L−1; silicate 20.3 μmol L−1) and Chl-a (2.17 μg L−1) than southern stations. Diatoms dominated (>90%), with centric forms peaking at Mumbai (322 988 cells L−1), pennate forms at Veraval (63 466 cells L−1) and Dinophyceae at Mangalore (8 432 cells L−1). Ecological indices indicated the highest richness at Mangalore (19 taxa), the highest diversity at Mumbai and Kanyakumari (H′ 1.9), and strong dominance at Veraval (H′ = 0.176, D = 0.940). The results demonstrate tight coupling between hydrography, nutrients and phytoplankton structure, highlighting the significance of spatial variability among stations and its implications for productivity and carbon cycling.
